results.title: "Overfed but Malnourished": Why Constant Snacking Isn't a Willpower Problem
results.description: We think snacking is just about hunger or a lack of willpower — but it's neither. In this conversation, functional medicine coach Tanya Malik Chawla unpacks why we really reach for food: it's part comfort, part habit made easier by quick commerce, and part a dopamine reward system that our body chases the same way it chases any addictive drug. The twist? Most people who snack constantly aren't overfed - they're malnourished, running low on protein, ferritin, and vitamin D even while eating all day. Tanya Malik Chawla compares the body to a car that's never refuelled or repaired, explaining why nonstop "grazing" leaves us running on empty no matter how much we eat. It's a reframe that finally makes sense of why cutting calories alone never seems to fix the cycle — and why the real fix starts with nutrition, not discipline.

results.title: What if you bought apple stock 10 years ago? Here’s what $10,000 would be worth today
results.description: Apple has created huge wealth for long-term investors. Apple is now worth about $4.54 trillion, after gaining roughly 51% in the past year. That increase added more than $1.5 trillion to the company’s market value. Apple was a much smaller company 10 years ago. In August 2016, Apple was worth about $580 billion. That means the value Apple added in just the past year is more than 2.5 times the company’s entire market value a decade ago, according to The Motley Fool.
